std-101-1.0:69E566CE-D8DB-5AD8-87EF-A78E.comment: The heading in section 1 uses lowercase for the word release while other sections use title case. For consistency across the document, the capitalization should be corrected.
std-101-1.0:69E566CE-D8DB-5AD8-87EF-A78E.proposedChange: Change release to Release in the final clause of the section.
std-101-1.0:69E566CE-D8DB-5AD8-87EF-A78E.response: The committee agrees with this editorial fix for consistency. The text will be updated to use title case for Release.

std-101-1.0:69E566CE-D8DB-5AD8-87EF-A78E.comment: As a supplier to many producers in New Zealand, I am concerned that holding batches for any review of minor log gaps will disrupt distribution schedules and increase warehouse costs without adding actual safety value.
std-101-1.0:69E566CE-D8DB-5AD8-87EF-A78E.response: The committee notes the concern regarding distribution delays, but maintaining rigorous batch check standards is essential for food safety and traceability of raw-milk cheese. No change is made.

std-101-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.comment: The section reference numbering should be checked for consistent bolding across all headings in the document to ensure clean publication formatting by the International Cheese Federation.
std-101-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.proposedChange: Bold the section number §1 consistently across the document headers.
std-101-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.response: The committee accepts this editorial improvement for document formatting consistency.

std-101-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.comment: The punctuation in §2 can be streamlined by adding a comma after the temperature range clause to improve readability for producers reviewing the aging minimums.
std-101-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.response: The committee accepts this editorial revision to improve sentence flow and readability.

std-101-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.comment: The list of conditions in §3 should use a semicolon before the final clause to separate the cleaning schedule requirement clearly from the logging requirement.
std-101-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.proposedChange: Insert a semicolon after raw-milk cheese in §3.
std-101-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.response: The committee accepts this editorial correction to clarify the separation of requirements within §3.

std-101-1.0:8010857E-9CEF-56E7-8879-A72A.comment: At Quincewick Creamery Cooperative, we suggest capitalizing ICF Member Producers to maintain professional styling throughout the definitions paragraph.
std-101-1.0:8010857E-9CEF-56E7-8879-A72A.response: The committee accepts this editorial suggestion to enhance the formal presentation of member designations.

std-101-1.0:8010857E-9CEF-56E7-8879-A72A.comment: The temperature scale notation in section 2 lists Fahrenheit first followed by Celsius. For international standardization, we should ensure the degree symbols and spacing match standard metric formatting.
std-101-1.0:8010857E-9CEF-56E7-8879-A72A.proposedChange: Ensure space and degree formatting reads as 35°F (1.7°C) consistently.
std-101-1.0:8010857E-9CEF-56E7-8879-A72A.response: The committee accepts the editorial correction to ensure proper formatting of temperature units across the document.

std-101-1.0:8010857E-9CEF-56E7-8879-A72A.comment: The wording referring to make record in section 4 should be pluralized to match batch documentation practices where multiple records may apply.
std-101-1.0:8010857E-9CEF-56E7-8879-A72A.proposedChange: Change make record to make records.
std-101-1.0:8010857E-9CEF-56E7-8879-A72A.response: The committee accepts this editorial clarification to reflect standard documentation practices accurately.

std-101-1.0:A93AF7D8-78BB-53A8-BA92-DFFF.comment: Retail buyers need more assurance that aging rooms maintain their conditions consistently. Requiring continuous automated temperature and humidity logging alongside daily checks would greatly help us verify the provenance of imported raw-milk cheeses.
std-101-1.0:A93AF7D8-78BB-53A8-BA92-DFFF.proposedChange: Add a requirement for continuous electronic logging in addition to daily manual checks.
std-101-1.0:A93AF7D8-78BB-53A8-BA92-DFFF.response: The committee accepts the principle of enhancing log verification. While §2 and §3 require daily checks and logging, guidance will be added in the upcoming annual conference materials to encourage continuous digital logging systems.

std-101-1.0:D8D82DD1-6AE6-571C-AEFC-7377.comment: Here at Fallowfen Cheese & Provisions, we noticed a minor typo in the definition list where make date lacks a hyphen. Adding the hyphen aligns with standard dairy terminology in Europe.
std-101-1.0:D8D82DD1-6AE6-571C-AEFC-7377.proposedChange: Insert a hyphen so make date reads make-date where appropriate.
std-101-1.0:D8D82DD1-6AE6-571C-AEFC-7377.response: The committee accepts this editorial correction to improve terminology clarity throughout the scope and definitions section.

std-101-1.0:EC981BB1-1AFE-5B09-93C4-BC11.comment: The phrasing in section 1 refers to unpasteurized milk, but export markets often require explicit mention of raw milk. To avoid confusion for international trade, the terminology should be standardized.
std-101-1.0:EC981BB1-1AFE-5B09-93C4-BC11.proposedChange: Replace unpasteurized milk with raw milk in the opening clause of §1.
std-101-1.0:EC981BB1-1AFE-5B09-93C4-BC11.response: The committee agrees that using raw milk provides better clarity for international trade and aligns with the document title. The text is updated accordingly.

std-101-1.1:62608AFC-06B4-5753-B0D3-688E.comment: At Aspenholt Dairy we train apprentices on transport logs. Simply referencing the daily log is insufficient because transport drivers also need to sign off on transfer temperatures to ensure no cold-chain interruption breaks the aging window before arrival at the secondary facility.
std-101-1.1:62608AFC-06B4-5753-B0D3-688E.proposedChange: Modify the text to require both the continuation of the daily log and the inclusion of transport driver temperature verification signatures during transfer.
std-101-1.1:62608AFC-06B4-5753-B0D3-688E.response: The committee agrees that transport temperatures must be documented during any off-site move. We have accepted the concern in principle by adding a requirement that transport manifests accompany the daily log to verify the cold chain remains intact.

std-101-1.1:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.comment: As Cheese Program Director at Herrera Farmstead, I approve the amendment allowing off-site aging continuity. However, the phrasing contains a minor typo where daily log is uncapitalized despite referring to a specific controlled record defined earlier in the standard.
std-101-1.1:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.proposedChange: Capitalize the words daily log to read Daily Log for consistency with the defined document titles in the main standard.
std-101-1.1:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.response: The committee appreciates the careful proofreading from Herrera Farmstead. The suggestion has been accepted, and the text in Amendment 1 now capitalizes Daily Log to maintain document-wide consistency with our defined terminology.

std-101-2.0-r1:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9.comment: Allowing two peer reviewers instead of an outside expert introduces too much variability in how environmental Listeria controls are evaluated across different ripening rooms.
std-101-2.0-r1:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9.proposedChange: Mandate that at least one of the two reviewers be an external food safety professional.
std-101-2.0-r1:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9.response: The committee rejects this proposal. The dual peer review option provides a practical and rigorous mechanism for members while maintaining appropriate oversight of raw-milk aging protocols.

std-101-2.0-r1:2266EC81-CDCD-5C2D-A2DC-4.comment: Requiring the first validation to be completed within a year places a heavy burden on smaller operations like Vandermolen Farmstead Creamery. Securing an outside expert or scheduling peers within twelve months disrupts our active production cycles.
std-101-2.0-r1:2266EC81-CDCD-5C2D-A2DC-4.proposedChange: Extend the deadline for the initial written protocol validation to eighteen months from the date of publication.
std-101-2.0-r1:2266EC81-CDCD-5C2D-A2DC-4.response: The committee recognizes the scheduling pressures placed on smaller producers during the initial rollout. While we are not extending the timeline to eighteen months, we have added a provision allowing a six-month grace period upon formal request to the committee.

std-101-2.0-r1:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7.comment: Allowing peer reviewers from an ICF list without any explicit conflict-of-interest exclusion leaves the validation process open to bias. Reviewers who have commercial ties to the producer should be barred from signing off on the aging protocol.
std-101-2.0-r1:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7.proposedChange: Add: Peer reviewers must not have any financial or commercial relationship with the producer whose protocol they are reviewing.
std-101-2.0-r1:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7.response: The committee agrees that impartiality is essential for credible peer reviews. The text is amended to explicitly bar peer reviewers with commercial ties to the evaluated producer.

std-101-2.0-r1:52640EB6-BBD5-5EA2-BDF1-1.comment: The current draft lacks a clear definition of what constitutes a valid protocol document. Producers need a defined template or minimum content checklist to ensure consistency before submission.
std-101-2.0-r1:52640EB6-BBD5-5EA2-BDF1-1.proposedChange: Add: The written protocol must include temperature logs, humidity controls, and pathogen testing schedules.
std-101-2.0-r1:52640EB6-BBD5-5EA2-BDF1-1.response: The committee agrees and will incorporate a standardized minimum content outline for the written protocol to ensure all submissions meet baseline safety and documentation expectations.

std-101-2.0-r1:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C.comment: Relying on peer reviewers from an ICF list does not go far enough. Retailers need assurance that all validators hold formal food safety accreditations rather than just peer status.
std-101-2.0-r1:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C.proposedChange: Require all peer reviewers to hold an accredited food safety certification alongside their ICF membership.
std-101-2.0-r1:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C.response: The committee rejects this change because peer reviewers are chosen for their practical expertise in raw-milk aging rather than mandatory third-party auditing credentials, which would add excessive cost.

std-101-2.0-r1:6B4BF43A-4C16-5DAD-9EA3-F.comment: As an educator, I see that members are confused about where to find the official ICF list of peer reviewers. Without a referenced location, trainees and small producers will struggle to comply with this standard.
std-101-2.0-r1:6B4BF43A-4C16-5DAD-9EA3-F.proposedChange: Add: The ICF list of qualified peer reviewers shall be maintained and published on the official member portal.
std-101-2.0-r1:6B4BF43A-4C16-5DAD-9EA3-F.response: The committee accepts this in principle and will ensure that instructions for accessing the ICF peer reviewer roster are clearly published in the guidance notes accompanying the standard.

std-101-2.0-r1:76CCF685-6B52-574A-A0A7-A.comment: Teaching raw-milk cheese aging principles at Aspenholt Farm requires absolute clarity on who qualifies as an outside expert versus a peer reviewer. The current draft blurs the qualifications and leaves too much room for subjective interpretation.
std-101-2.0-r1:76CCF685-6B52-574A-A0A7-A.proposedChange: Define an outside expert as a certified dairy scientist or food safety auditor with at least five years of commercial raw-milk aging experience.
std-101-2.0-r1:76CCF685-6B52-574A-A0A7-A.response: The committee acknowledges the need for precise definitions in educational settings. We have incorporated specific credentialing guidelines for outside experts, specifying relevant professional experience in dairy science to guide members and educators properly.

std-101-2.0-r1:AC73CCD5-783B-5A03-9A6B-3.comment: At Pippinvale Farm we worry that the peer review route lacks any explicit conflict-of-interest safeguard. Two peers from the ICF list could easily be business partners or trade rivals, which compromises the integrity of our aging protocol validation.
std-101-2.0-r1:AC73CCD5-783B-5A03-9A6B-3.proposedChange: Add a sentence requiring peer reviewers to sign a conflict-of-interest declaration stating they have no financial ties to the evaluated creamery.
std-101-2.0-r1:AC73CCD5-783B-5A03-9A6B-3.response: The committee agrees that impartiality must be guaranteed for all peer reviewers. We have accepted the principle of this objection and added a mandatory conflict-of-interest disclosure requirement for all peers on the ICF list, ensuring unbiased reviews before validation is finalized.

std-101-2.0-r1:CCC015AC-1247-5EA6-A662-F.comment: The reference to the ICF list is helpful, but the wording can be smoothed out to make the review pathway easier to read for busy creamery staff.
std-101-2.0-r1:CCC015AC-1247-5EA6-A662-F.proposedChange: Change reviewed every three years by an outside expert or by two peer reviewers from an ICF list to reviewed triennially by an outside expert or two qualified ICF peer reviewers.
std-101-2.0-r1:CCC015AC-1247-5EA6-A662-F.response: The committee accepts the proposed wording change as it enhances readability without altering the underlying technical requirements of the review process.

std-101-2.0-r1:CCFA1913-AF56-545A-B63A-3.comment: At Crowfeather Creamery, we find the three-year review cycle too rigid given seasonal batch variations. A fixed triennial review does not account for temporary cave renovations or milk supply shifts that happen naturally.
std-101-2.0-r1:CCFA1913-AF56-545A-B63A-3.proposedChange: Change triennial review to every three years or upon any major structural modification to the aging facility.
std-101-2.0-r1:CCFA1913-AF56-545A-B63A-3.response: The committee has addressed this concern by adding language that clarifies reviews may also be triggered by significant facility modifications, aligning the schedule with practical operational realities.

std-101-2.0-r1:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C.comment: The section heading and opening sentence are slightly disconnected regarding the distinction between initial validation and subsequent reviews. Adding a hyphen to the term written protocol improves clarity.
std-101-2.0-r1:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C.proposedChange: Change written protocol to formally documented protocol.
std-101-2.0-r1:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C.response: The committee accepts the editorial correction to improve clarity and maintain consistent terminology throughout the document.

std-101-2.0-r1:FB0FA9E7-BEB6-5525-86E5-E.comment: Requiring the first validation to be completed within a year places an undue financial and administrative burden on small-scale affineurs like Herrera Farmstead. We need a longer transition period to arrange outside experts without disrupting our aging schedules.
std-101-2.0-r1:FB0FA9E7-BEB6-5525-86E5-E.response: The committee recognizes the tight timeline for existing producers. The implementation window for the initial validation is extended to two years to allow adequate preparation.

std-101-2.0-r1:FBB1722E-F036-5279-BD6C-F.comment: The requirement for an outside expert every three years will disproportionately penalize small artisan producers due to high consultant fees and travel expenses.
std-101-2.0-r1:FBB1722E-F036-5279-BD6C-F.proposedChange: Exempt producers aging fewer than five thousand wheels annually from the outside expert requirement.
std-101-2.0-r1:FBB1722E-F036-5279-BD6C-F.response: The committee declines the exemption because safety validation standards must apply consistently to raw-milk cheese aging regardless of production volume to protect public health.

std-101-2.0-r1:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7.comment: As a retailer receiving cheese from various producers, Wrenfield Creamery relies on consistent documentation. The three-year review cycle is sensible, but the text fails to state how retailers or inspectors can verify that the protocol was actually reviewed.
std-101-2.0-r1:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7.proposedChange: Require creamery operators to display a validation stamp or date on their batch documentation indicating the last peer review or expert check.
std-101-2.0-r1:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7.response: The committee agrees that traceability and verification are essential for market confidence. We have accepted the proposal to require a visible validation date and reviewer identifier on all protocol summary records kept for inspection.

std-101-2.0-r2:2266EC81-CDCD-5C2D-A2DC-4.comment: Representing Vandermolen Farmstead Creamery, I am concerned that allowing one validation to cover close variants is too vague without defining specific moisture and pH thresholds, which leaves too much room for subjective interpretation by peer reviewers during audits.
std-101-2.0-r2:2266EC81-CDCD-5C2D-A2DC-4.proposedChange: Insert specific criteria stating that close variants must remain within plus or minus 2 percent moisture and 0.15 pH of the master protocol.
std-101-2.0-r2:2266EC81-CDCD-5C2D-A2DC-4.response: The committee accepts the technical critique regarding vague variant definitions. We have incorporated explicit quantitative thresholds for moisture and pH to ensure consistent evaluation by peer reviewers across all certified facilities.

std-101-2.0-r2:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7.comment: As a retailer, I support the conflict-of-interest rules for peer reviewers added in this revision. However, the cross-reference pointing to the definitions section uses an incorrect paragraph number, which could cause confusion when auditing supplier documentation.
std-101-2.0-r2:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7.proposedChange: Update the cross-reference from section 1.4 to section 1.5.
std-101-2.0-r2:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7.response: The committee accepts this editorial correction. The cross-reference to the definitions section has been verified and updated to reference section 1.5 as requested.

std-101-2.0-r2:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C.comment: Speaking as counter lead at Ostergaard's Cheese Shop, giving producers two years is fine, but import requirements and foreign compliance timelines still do not align smoothly with this schedule, creating unnecessary administrative friction for imported raw-milk artisan cheeses coming onto our retail shelves.
std-101-2.0-r2:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C.response: The committee rejects this general comment. The code addresses domestic and international raw-milk aging practices under standard validation frameworks and cannot alter external import regulations or foreign compliance schedules outside its direct scope.

std-101-2.0-r2:CCFA1913-AF56-545A-B63A-3.comment: As head cheesemaker at Crowfeather Creamery, I find the two-year period to validate our first protocol helpful, but the text fails to specify if minor moisture adjustments during affinage require restarting the entire two-year clock. We need explicit wording protecting standard adjustments.
std-101-2.0-r2:CCFA1913-AF56-545A-B63A-3.proposedChange: Add a sentence stating that standard moisture adjustments during ongoing aging do not restart the two-year validation window.
std-101-2.0-r2:CCFA1913-AF56-545A-B63A-3.response: The committee notes the concern regarding routine moisture adjustments during aging. While the exact proposed wording is adjusted for drafting style, we have inserted clarifying text ensuring that standard adjustments during affinage do not trigger a reset of the two-year validation period.

std-101-2.0-r2:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C.comment: At Quillbrook Dairy Institute, we welcome the two-year validation window, but the wording about close variants contains a dangling hyphen in the compound adjective 'close-variant'. Fixing this minor typographical error will ensure clear reading across all of our production rooms during daily shifts.
std-101-2.0-r2:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C.response: The committee agrees that editorial precision aids clarity. The text has been updated to use the hyphenated form 'close-variant' as suggested by the production lead.

std-101-2.0:067065F5-7F1C-57F1-A0F8-92D7.comment: As a cheese program director at Hazelcombe Cheesemonger, I support the requirement for validated aging protocols in §3, but the section needs a clear definition of what constitutes an acceptable outside expert to guide retailers and producers when selecting reviewers.
std-101-2.0:067065F5-7F1C-57F1-A0F8-92D7.proposedChange: Add a descriptive sentence in §3 defining an outside expert as an independent food scientist or professional affineur with at least five years of raw-milk experience.
std-101-2.0:067065F5-7F1C-57F1-A0F8-92D7.response: The committee accepts the comment. Section 3 has been updated to include a clear definition specifying the professional background and experience required for outside experts reviewing aging protocols.

std-101-2.0:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9D48.comment: As a food safety consultant advising Fernholt Dairy, I suggest clarifying the term temperature excursion in the release checks clause so producers know exactly what degree threshold triggers testing. A precise definition avoids confusion during audits and ensures consistent safety verification across all batches.
std-101-2.0:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9D48.proposedChange: Define temperature excursion in §4 as any deviation exceeding 40 degrees Fahrenheit for more than four continuous hours.
std-101-2.0:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9D48.response: The committee agrees that defining temperature excursion provides clarity for producers. We have updated §4 to include the suggested threshold for continuous deviation, ensuring consistent application of the release check protocol across all member operations.

std-101-2.0:238F296A-96BC-5E37-AB6D-6BC0.comment: At Thistlemere Dairy Systems, the three-year outside review requirement does not account for micro-creameries that lack external advisory budgets. We need a provision for peer evaluation groups.
std-101-2.0:238F296A-96BC-5E37-AB6D-6BC0.proposedChange: Insert: or a certified peer review committee recognized by the ICF after each three-year cycle.
std-101-2.0:238F296A-96BC-5E37-AB6D-6BC0.response: The committee accepts this proposal. Recognizing ICF-recognized peer review committees provides a practical, community-driven pathway for compliance without compromising technical oversight.

std-101-2.0:38462C1A-999E-520E-BE56-FA3F.comment: Operating as an affineur in Portugal, I believe the three-year outside review cycle in §3 fails to account for traditional multi-generational caves where aging dynamics remain perfectly stable over decades. A rigid triennial review mandate disregards proven historical practices.
std-101-2.0:38462C1A-999E-520E-BE56-FA3F.proposedChange: Amend §3 to exempt traditional aging facilities with more than twenty years of documented compliance from the triennial outside review requirement.
std-101-2.0:38462C1A-999E-520E-BE56-FA3F.response: The committee accepts the principle that long-standing facilities demonstrate stability. We have revised §3 to allow facilities with over twenty years of documented compliance to undergo outside expert review every five years instead of three.

std-101-2.0:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7EEB.comment: The addition of washed-curd and stretched-curd styles is a wonderful update that helps retailers classify inventory properly. The section is clear, but a small typo fix in the punctuation will make it cleaner.
std-101-2.0:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7EEB.proposedChange: Remove the trailing semicolon after stretched-curd styles and replace with a period.
std-101-2.0:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7EEB.response: The committee accepts this editorial correction. Punctuation has been updated for consistency across all definitions in the scope.

std-101-2.0:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7EEB.comment: Retailers rely on consistent aging standards, but forcing small makers into costly third-party audits every three years will shrink product diversity. We should allow alternative verification methods.
std-101-2.0:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7EEB.proposedChange: Amend to permit peer review or accredited internal audits in lieu of outside expert review.
std-101-2.0:4106750C-D56C-5D58-8CDC-7EEB.response: The committee accepts this in principle. The revised draft will accommodate peer review options and technical guidance developed during chapter meet-ups, addressing cost concerns while maintaining safety.

std-101-2.0:52C28E21-26ED-505E-8B9A-D2BD.comment: At Rushfen Cheese & Provisions, the inclusion of washed-curd and stretched-curd styles is a great addition, but the cross-reference to ICF-STD-102 lacks specific subsection pointers. Adding the precise subsection will save our team time when cross-checking our record-keeping compliance during internal audits.
std-101-2.0:52C28E21-26ED-505E-8B9A-D2BD.proposedChange: Update the cross-reference in §2 to point specifically to subsection 3 of ICF-STD-102.
std-101-2.0:52C28E21-26ED-505E-8B9A-D2BD.response: The committee accepts the comment. The cross-reference in §2 has been updated to point directly to subsection 3 of ICF-STD-102 for improved clarity and ease of navigation during audits.

std-101-2.0:52C28E21-26ED-505E-8B9A-D2BD.comment: As creamery manager at Rushfen Cheese & Provisions, I find the minimum aging requirement of 60 days at 35 degrees Fahrenheit or above should explicitly mention that it aligns with the federal floor, to prevent any confusion among inspectors regarding state versus federal jurisdictions.
std-101-2.0:52C28E21-26ED-505E-8B9A-D2BD.proposedChange: Insert text into §3 noting that the 60-day minimum aging period aligns fully with the federal floor for raw-milk cheeses.
std-101-2.0:52C28E21-26ED-505E-8B9A-D2BD.response: The committee recognizes the importance of regulatory clarity. Although the text of §3 remains unchanged regarding the 60-day minimum, the accompanying guidelines will now explicitly note alignment with the federal floor to assist inspectors and producers.

std-101-2.0:52C28E21-26ED-505E-8B9A-D2BD.comment: The hold-and-test requirement in §5 is redundant because our existing quality assurance program already mandates microbiological testing after any significant temperature excursion during the aging process. Adding this mandate without acknowledging existing producer controls creates unnecessary paperwork.
std-101-2.0:52C28E21-26ED-505E-8B9A-D2BD.proposedChange: Remove the mandatory hold-and-test step in §5 for facilities that maintain an approved HACCP monitoring plan.
std-101-2.0:52C28E21-26ED-505E-8B9A-D2BD.response: The committee rejects this change. While we recognize that many members maintain robust HACCP plans, a uniform hold-and-test requirement following any temperature excursion is essential to guarantee consumer safety and maintain consistent standards across all raw-milk cheese producers.

std-101-2.0:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C6BF.comment: At Ostergaard's Cheese Shop in Oamaru, the inclusion of stretched-curd styles in §2 raises classification questions regarding specific regional pasta filata cheeses that do not neatly fit standard definitions. This requires careful alignment with international nomenclature before final adoption.
std-101-2.0:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C6BF.proposedChange: Defer the addition of stretched-curd styles in §2 until a comprehensive international survey of pasta filata definitions is completed.
std-101-2.0:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C6BF.response: The committee has decided to defer this specific comment for consideration in the next revision cycle of the document, as the current definitions for washed-curd and stretched-curd styles were thoroughly vetted and approved by the majority of the ballot pool.

std-101-2.0:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C6BF.comment: The minimum aging requirement of 60 days at 35 degrees Fahrenheit or above creates severe inventory bottlenecks for specialty retailers and small producers who rely on faster turnover for fresh-tasting raw-milk cheeses. The rule should provide seasonal flexibility for specific styles.
std-101-2.0:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C6BF.proposedChange: Add a provision in §3 allowing reduced aging periods for cheeses demonstrated to be safe through accredited pathogen challenge testing.
std-101-2.0:5E1DE6DE-303A-5B35-87D6-C6BF.response: The committee notes the concern regarding inventory turnover, but the 60-day minimum aging requirement is anchored in established safety parameters and the federal floor. However, the committee agrees to include guidance clarifying that challenge studies may be used under §3 for novel protocols.

std-101-2.0:65D40948-FA0D-5DB6-9F63-6AB6.comment: At Elderfen Farm, our aging room occasionally records brief ambient spikes when loading fresh wheels. Treating every minor chart deviation as a critical excursion requiring microbiological testing places an unfair burden on small-scale producers who already monitor humidity and core pH rigorously.
std-101-2.0:65D40948-FA0D-5DB6-9F63-6AB6.proposedChange: Clarify that excursions under two hours do not trigger mandatory batch testing if core temperature remains stable.
std-101-2.0:65D40948-FA0D-5DB6-9F63-6AB6.response: The committee rejected the comment because any recorded excursion outside the validated aging parameters warrants verification testing. Core temperature stability alone cannot guarantee surface pathogen suppression without a complete hold-and-test verification.

std-101-2.0:72A4DA25-C472-5D86-81EA-DDCF.comment: At Rushfen Creamery Cooperative, referencing ICF-STD-102 for our aging records creates administrative duplication since our digital inventory system already captures all required parameters. Replacing the old clauses without offering a streamlined integration path places an unnecessary burden on cooperative members managing multiple production lines.
std-101-2.0:72A4DA25-C472-5D86-81EA-DDCF.proposedChange: Add an exemption clause in §5 allowing validated digital ERP systems to serve in place of standard ICF-STD-102 record forms.
std-101-2.0:72A4DA25-C472-5D86-81EA-DDCF.response: The committee acknowledges the administrative burden on cooperatives utilizing digital systems. While §5 maintains the reference to ICF-STD-102 for uniformity, we have added a clarifying note permitting equivalent electronic logs that meet the data capture requirements of the referenced standard.

std-101-2.0:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.comment: Mandating an outside expert review every three years imposes a severe financial burden on farmstead producers and smaller regional creameries. Many craft makers operate on tight margins and cannot easily absorb third-party consulting fees without raising retail prices significantly across our distribution network.
std-101-2.0:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.proposedChange: Replace the mandatory outside expert review with a qualified peer review option every three years.
std-101-2.0:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.response: The committee accepted the comment in principle. While independent validation remains necessary, the requirement will be revised to allow qualified peer review panels alongside outside experts to ease the financial burden on small producers.

std-101-2.0:75F3B7F3-5CE6-5E42-9EE3-76A4.comment: Our creamery operates in a climate where ambient seasonal shifts make maintaining 35°F (1.7°C) challenging without substantial capital upgrades. We need to align this with regional variances permitted under the federal floor.
std-101-2.0:75F3B7F3-5CE6-5E42-9EE3-76A4.proposedChange: Insert a tolerance of plus or minus 2 degrees Fahrenheit for aging room minimum temperature limits.
std-101-2.0:75F3B7F3-5CE6-5E42-9EE3-76A4.response: The committee deferred the comment for future study by the technical subcommittee, noting that aging temperature minimums are critical for pathogen inhibition and cannot be adjusted without safety review.

std-101-2.0:75F3B7F3-5CE6-5E42-9EE3-76A4.comment: The requirement for written validation protocols and outside expert review imposes an administrative load that diverts our limited creamery staff away from cheese production. Smaller operations should be entirely exempt.
std-101-2.0:75F3B7F3-5CE6-5E42-9EE3-76A4.proposedChange: Exempt all production facilities processing under fifty thousand liters annually from the outside expert review requirement.
std-101-2.0:75F3B7F3-5CE6-5E42-9EE3-76A4.response: The committee rejected the comment because food safety validation is essential for all raw-milk cheeses regardless of production volume, though accommodations for peer review have been introduced elsewhere.

std-101-2.0:772B55A8-44C7-51C3-8BEE-37B9.comment: At Pippinvale Dairy Institute, requiring an outside expert review every three years imposes a rigid burden that ignores internal validation competency. We need to allow peer review or qualified internal quality teams to satisfy this clause.
std-101-2.0:772B55A8-44C7-51C3-8BEE-37B9.proposedChange: Replace outside expert with qualified peer review or internal quality validation every three years.
std-101-2.0:772B55A8-44C7-51C3-8BEE-37B9.response: The committee accepts this proposal. Allowing qualified peer review alongside outside experts provides sufficient rigor for validating aging protocols while easing the financial burden on smaller member producers.

std-101-2.0:856688F8-C895-5E8E-91F2-CDF1.comment: Requiring an outside expert to review aging protocols every three years imposes an unreasonable financial burden on small-scale producers like us in Ithaca. Peer review by qualified cheesemakers within our ICF chapter should be permitted as a cost-effective and rigorous alternative to expensive commercial consultants.
std-101-2.0:856688F8-C895-5E8E-91F2-CDF1.proposedChange: Revise §3 to allow a qualified peer review committee from the local ICF chapter to fulfill the three-year validation requirement.
std-101-2.0:856688F8-C895-5E8E-91F2-CDF1.response: The committee accepts the proposal. Section 3 has been revised to permit qualified peer review by trained members of an ICF chapter, reducing costs for smaller makers while maintaining rigorous scientific oversight of aging protocols.

std-101-2.0:8EA56787-CF23-5ED9-A4A0-0DEF.comment: As a retail manager receiving raw-milk cheeses from various makers, I appreciate having standardized protocols to review. However, the cross-reference to the outside expert review lacks a specific section number, which makes verifying compliance cumbersome during our intake audits. Adding the proper subsection reference will clarify this obligation.
std-101-2.0:8EA56787-CF23-5ED9-A4A0-0DEF.proposedChange: Change the reference to read as §3.2 for outside expert review requirements.
std-101-2.0:8EA56787-CF23-5ED9-A4A0-0DEF.response: The committee accepted the comment because clarifying cross-references assists supply chain transparency and retail intake verification. The draft will be updated to include the exact subsection pointer before recirculation.

std-101-2.0:8EA56787-CF23-5ED9-A4A0-0DEF.comment: The requirement to hold and test any batch experiencing a temperature excursion is too rigid for retail distribution centers. Minor fluctuations during transport or short display case cycles do not necessarily compromise raw-milk safety, and mandatory testing for every minor blip will disrupt our inventory flow and increase costs unnecessarily.
std-101-2.0:8EA56787-CF23-5ED9-A4A0-0DEF.proposedChange: Limit the hold-and-test requirement to temperature excursions exceeding four hours cumulative duration.
std-101-2.0:8EA56787-CF23-5ED9-A4A0-0DEF.response: The committee rejected the comment because temperature excursions directly impact pathogen control during raw-milk cheese aging. Maintaining strict hold-and-test triggers is essential for consumer safety, regardless of distribution scale.

std-101-2.0:958B1085-3310-588F-AAC0-31AA.comment: The mandate for outside expert review every three years is too restrictive for small producers who operate on tight margins. Peer review should be explicitly accepted as an equivalent mechanism.
std-101-2.0:958B1085-3310-588F-AAC0-31AA.proposedChange: Change outside expert every three years to outside expert or peer review group every three years.
std-101-2.0:958B1085-3310-588F-AAC0-31AA.response: The committee accepts this in principle. The text will be revised to permit peer reviews conducted under ICF guidelines, balancing affordability with rigorous technical oversight.

std-101-2.0:965ED95C-59D7-55DE-AA49-FCC9.comment: At Cindervale Fine Cheese, we find the inclusion of stretched-curd raw-milk styles creates ambiguity regarding moisture levels and pathogen persistence during aging. The scope should restrict these styles until further data is published.
std-101-2.0:965ED95C-59D7-55DE-AA49-FCC9.proposedChange: Remove stretched-curd styles from the scope until additional pathogen validation studies are completed by the technical committee.
std-101-2.0:965ED95C-59D7-55DE-AA49-FCC9.response: The committee rejected the comment because stretched-curd raw-milk cheeses have a long history of safe production and are adequately covered by the validation protocols in §3 and release checks in §4.

std-101-2.0:976770B1-F266-55ED-94DB-0D2C.comment: The text outlining the validation frequency could be improved for better readability. Using bullet points for the review intervals and documentation steps would help producers understand their obligations at a glance.
std-101-2.0:976770B1-F266-55ED-94DB-0D2C.proposedChange: Reformat the second paragraph of §3 into a bulleted list outlining the three-year validation cycle and documentation requirements.
std-101-2.0:976770B1-F266-55ED-94DB-0D2C.response: The committee accepted the editorial suggestion to format the review intervals as a bulleted list, enhancing readability and ease of compliance for all member producers.

std-101-2.0:A7494213-EBF3-5A89-8197-8657.comment: As a retailer, I support including washed and stretched curd styles. However, the cross-reference to ICF-STD-102 should explicitly mention that it covers record retention periods so that buyers andmongers know what to look for when auditing suppliers.
std-101-2.0:A7494213-EBF3-5A89-8197-8657.proposedChange: Change the reference to read: points to ICF-STD-102 for records and retention schedules.
std-101-2.0:A7494213-EBF3-5A89-8197-8657.response: The committee accepts the spirit of this comment in part. While we agree clarity is helpful, explicitly adding retention schedules here duplicates the scope of ICF-STD-102. We have adjusted the wording slightly to ensure seamless cross-referencing without redundancy.

std-101-2.0:AC73CCD5-783B-5A03-9A6B-3A97.comment: At Pippinvale Farm, we find the phrasing regarding validation protocols slightly ambiguous. We should ensure the text specifically notes that protocols must account for seasonal milk variations during the aging lifecycle.
std-101-2.0:AC73CCD5-783B-5A03-9A6B-3A97.proposedChange: Add the phrase accounting for seasonal milk variations to the first sentence.
std-101-2.0:AC73CCD5-783B-5A03-9A6B-3A97.response: The committee accepts this proposal. Incorporating seasonal variations strengthens the validation requirement and aligns with best practices discussed at recent ICF webinars.

std-101-2.0:B2A26737-D6CB-5149-8848-01C2.comment: The current wording specifies 35°F (1.7°C) or above, which is clear, but adding an explicit note regarding freezing prevention would help new herd managers operating cold aging rooms.
std-101-2.0:B2A26737-D6CB-5149-8848-01C2.proposedChange: Add a brief advisory note: 'Care must be taken to prevent freezing of the cheese matrix during aging.'
std-101-2.0:B2A26737-D6CB-5149-8848-01C2.response: The committee accepted the addition as a helpful practical clarification for cheese producers managing cold-room setpoints.

std-101-2.0:B2A26737-D6CB-5149-8848-01C2.comment: At Pinebarrow Creamery, holding an entire batch due to a minor, brief temperature fluctuation on a single sensor is overly punitive and ignores the thermal mass of large wheels. We need a risk-based waiver for brief spikes.
std-101-2.0:B2A26737-D6CB-5149-8848-01C2.proposedChange: Add an exemption clause for temperature spikes lasting less than sixty minutes if core cheese temperature remains within safe limits.
std-101-2.0:B2A26737-D6CB-5149-8848-01C2.response: The committee deferred this comment to the next revision cycle, noting that further technical study is required before creating exemptions to mandatory hold-and-test rules.

std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.comment: The expanded scope mentioning washed-curd and stretched-curd styles creates a pedagogical mismatch with our training materials taught in association courses. We need a clearer demarcation of moisture thresholds in the definitions so educators can properly instruct students on raw-milk aging classifications.
std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.proposedChange: Incorporate specific moisture percentage ranges for washed-curd and stretched-curd styles directly into the definitions paragraph.
std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.response: The committee rejected the comment because exact moisture thresholds vary widely across traditional styles and are better addressed in guidance documents rather than the core standard's scope definitions.

std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.comment: Requiring an outside expert review every three years places an undue financial burden on our smaller artisan cheesemakers and member facilities. We should permit a structured peer-review option or extend the cycle for smaller producers to ensure participation without compromising our safety goals.
std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.proposedChange: Amend §3 to allow a qualified peer-review process conducted by trained ICF members every three years as an alternative to commercial outside experts.
std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.response: The committee accepted the comment because smaller producers raised valid cost concerns during the ballot. Section 3 is revised to permit documented peer review by qualified ICF members every three years for facilities producing under a set volume.

std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.comment: To maintain clarity when training staff and auditing aging facilities, we should explicitly cross-reference the exact section on temperature logs in ICF-STD-102 so there is no confusion.
std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.proposedChange: Add the phrase 'referencing ICF-STD-102 for log requirements' at the end of the paragraph.
std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.response: The committee accepted the editorial correction to improve cross-document clarity and alignment with the new records standard.

std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.comment: The pointer to ICF-STD-102 is clear, but we should add a direct mention of the retention period for digital logs to assist educators and students using this code.
std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.proposedChange: Insert 'including digital and paper logs retained for five years' into the sentence.
std-101-2.0:BA129EA6-B517-5C25-9F0D-D2D5.response: The committee rejected this change because specific retention periods and formats are fully detailed in ICF-STD-102, and repeating them here would create redundancy.

std-101-2.0:CCFA1913-AF56-545A-B63A-3916.comment: At Crowfeather Creamery, we appreciate the hold-and-test requirement for temperature excursions. However, the term excursion needs a clearer threshold so we know exactly which degree variance triggers the mandatory hold.
std-101-2.0:CCFA1913-AF56-545A-B63A-3916.proposedChange: Clarify 'temperature excursion' to mean any recorded reading exceeding 45°F (7.2°C) for more than two consecutive hours.
std-101-2.0:CCFA1913-AF56-545A-B63A-3916.response: The committee accepted the proposed change to define the temperature excursion threshold clearly, ensuring consistent application across all aging facilities.

std-101-2.0:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C6F2.comment: Mandating external validation reviews every three years will force Quillbrook Dairy Institute to redirect critical capital away from our caves and make operations unnecessarily expensive for craft producers.
std-101-2.0:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C6F2.response: The committee rejects this general comment because independent validation is essential to consumer safety and public trust in raw-milk cheeses. The cost is outweighed by the risk reduction for the sector.

std-101-2.0:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C6F2.comment: Replacing the old record clauses with a clean reference to ICF-STD-102 is great for readability, but we should make sure the section heading clearly indicates that aging records are governed externally by that document.
std-101-2.0:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C6F2.proposedChange: Change heading to read: §5 Aging records (see ICF-STD-102).
std-101-2.0:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C6F2.response: The committee accepts this editorial change. Adding the parenthetical note to the heading improves navigation and immediately directs members to the correct standard.

std-101-2.0:EC981BB1-1AFE-5B09-93C4-BC11.comment: As a cheese buyer, I rely on rigorous independent oversight. Allowing peer reviews instead of outside experts for validated aging protocols would weaken consumer confidence and undermine the integrity of raw-milk safety standards.
std-101-2.0:EC981BB1-1AFE-5B09-93C4-BC11.proposedChange: Modify §3 to explicitly restrict validation reviews exclusively to certified commercial outside experts, removing any language permitting peer review.
std-101-2.0:EC981BB1-1AFE-5B09-93C4-BC11.response: The committee rejected this comment because the revised §3 balances expert oversight with a peer-review option to accommodate the diverse operational scales of our membership while maintaining strict safety validation.

std-101-2.0:FB0FA9E7-BEB6-5525-86E5-E580.comment: As an affineur working with diverse raw-milk batches, I find the triennial outside review requirement overly prescriptive and costly for small ripening rooms. Allowing alternative validation pathways, such as peer review or documented historical pathogen reduction data, would better serve our community without sacrificing food safety standards.
std-101-2.0:FB0FA9E7-BEB6-5525-86E5-E580.proposedChange: Amend §3 to permit peer review or historical batch safety data as acceptable equivalents to outside expert review.
std-101-2.0:FB0FA9E7-BEB6-5525-86E5-E580.response: The committee accepted the comment because incorporating peer review and documented historical safety data offers a practical alternative while maintaining rigorous oversight of raw-milk aging protocols.

std-101-2.0:FB0FA9E7-BEB6-5525-86E5-E580.comment: The release check clause is generally sound, but the terminology referring to temperature excursions could be more precise to align with standard data logger outputs. Specifying that the log must reflect continuous monitoring will prevent ambiguity during audits.
std-101-2.0:FB0FA9E7-BEB6-5525-86E5-E580.proposedChange: Insert the word continuous before monitoring in the first sentence of §4.
std-101-2.0:FB0FA9E7-BEB6-5525-86E5-E580.response: The committee accepted the editorial change to improve clarity regarding data logger requirements and ensure consistent interpretation across all certified aging facilities.

std-101-2.0:FBB1722E-F036-5279-BD6C-F190.comment: At Larkhollow Dairy Systems, we welcome the expanded scope. To ensure complete clarity for producers transitioning to these new styles, we should add a brief clarifying phrase.
std-101-2.0:FBB1722E-F036-5279-BD6C-F190.proposedChange: Insert including traditional formats after stretched-curd styles in the first sentence.
std-101-2.0:FBB1722E-F036-5279-BD6C-F190.response: The committee accepts this proposal. The added phrase clarifies the intended scope for washed-curd and stretched-curd cheeses without changing the core definition.

std-101-2.0:FBB1722E-F036-5279-BD6C-F190.comment: As an owner at Larkhollow Dairy Systems, I welcome the added clarity on washed-curd and stretched-curd styles. However, the cross-reference to ICF-STD-102 for records uses an outdated section numbering style. We should fix this typo before final publication to ensure clear guidance for all members.
std-101-2.0:FBB1722E-F036-5279-BD6C-F190.proposedChange: Update the cross-reference to read ICF-STD-102 Section 4 for records.
std-101-2.0:FBB1722E-F036-5279-BD6C-F190.response: The committee agrees with the commenter that the cross-reference needed correction for clarity and ease of use. The text has been updated to cite ICF-STD-102 Section 4 directly as proposed.

std-101-2.0:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7BE8.comment: The inclusion of washed-curd and stretched-curd styles in the scope is a welcome update for mongers handling diverse inventories. However, the wording should explicitly mention that these styles remain subject to the baseline aging timeframe to avoid any confusion among importers.
std-101-2.0:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7BE8.proposedChange: Add a clarifying sentence stating that all newly included styles are subject to the minimum aging requirements in §2.
std-101-2.0:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7BE8.response: The committee accepted the comment in principle. Rather than adding a duplicate restriction in §1, the committee will cross-reference §2 directly within the scope definitions to ensure absolute clarity.

std-101-2.0:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7BE8.comment: The proposed requirement for outside expert review every three years introduces unnecessary administrative overhead and increases costs for imported raw-milk selections. Retailers rely on steady producer output, and overly complex validation hurdles risk reducing the availability of traditional cheeses.
std-101-2.0:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7BE8.proposedChange: Delete the requirement for outside expert review and rely solely on the federal floor for aging safety.
std-101-2.0:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7BE8.response: The committee rejected the comment because relying solely on the federal floor does not fulfill the association's commitment to self-regulation and validated aging protocols for raw-milk cheeses.

std-102-1.0:2980EAB2-2260-5C34-9828-158B.comment: In our educational programming, we teach producers that two years of record retention following the final sale of a batch aligns well with standard commercial shelf-life expectations for aged cheeses. However, for short-aged fresh cheeses sold within days, holding records for two full years creates excessive storage overhead. A tiered retention schedule based on cheese category would better serve our membership.
std-102-1.0:2980EAB2-2260-5C34-9828-158B.proposedChange: Revise §2 to specify a one-year retention for fresh cheeses and two years for aged cheeses sold after sixty days.
std-102-1.0:2980EAB2-2260-5C34-9828-158B.response: The committee accepted the comment in principle. A future guidance document will address tiered retention periods for fresh versus aged varieties, but the current two-year baseline remains appropriate for universal safety coverage across all standardized product types.

std-102-1.0:62608AFC-06B4-5753-B0D3-688E.comment: The wording in §3 is clear and concise regarding outsourced aging relationships. To ensure better grammatical flow between clauses, a minor comma adjustment will help members parse the responsibility between the affineur and the original maker.
std-102-1.0:62608AFC-06B4-5753-B0D3-688E.proposedChange: Insert a comma in §3 after the word member so it reads: When an affineur or another member ages the cheese, the maker keeps a copy of the aging log for each batch.
std-102-1.0:62608AFC-06B4-5753-B0D3-688E.response: The committee accepted the comment. The comma is added to improve sentence structure and clarity for readers navigating outsourced aging requirements.

std-102-1.0:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.comment: As a retailer receiving cheese from various collaborative aging programs, having clarity that the maker holds the master aging log copy provides great assurance. Capitalizing the term affineur is unnecessary and should be changed to lower case for consistency with the rest of the drafting style.
std-102-1.0:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.response: The committee accepted the comment. The capitalization is corrected to maintain consistent stylistic standards throughout the document.

std-102-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.comment: Reviewing §2 from a quality systems perspective, the phrase 'on paper or electronically' is clear, but adding 'format' immediately after helps align with standard document control terminology used across our manufacturing membership.
std-102-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.proposedChange: Amend §2 to read: on paper format or electronically.
std-102-1.0:78E29F46-3965-5314-BC2F-BB79.response: The committee accepted the comment. The addition of the word format improves readability and aligns the section with standard industry documentation terminology.

std-102-1.0:965ED95C-59D7-55DE-AA49-FCC9.comment: At Cindervale Fine Cheese, we frequently purchase batches that have been aged externally by independent affineurs. While we understand the intent to trace history, requiring the original maker to hold copies of every external aging log creates an impossible logistical burden when dealing with artisan facilities that lack integrated software. The third-party affineur should hold sole responsibility for their specific aging records without requiring duplicate copies to be sent back to the primary producer.
std-102-1.0:965ED95C-59D7-55DE-AA49-FCC9.proposedChange: Amend §3 to state that the affineur keeps the log and makes it available to the maker upon request.
std-102-1.0:965ED95C-59D7-55DE-AA49-FCC9.response: The committee rejected the comment. Keeping a copy of the aging log at the maker's facility is essential for complete batch traceability from milk source to release. Relying solely on external parties leaves makers vulnerable if an affineur ceases operations or misplaces records during extended maturation cycles.

std-102-1.0:CCC015AC-1247-5EA6-A662-FBE0.comment: At Nornbrook Cheesemonger, our make sheets capture multiple milk silos and varying culture inoculations across a single production day. Listing every single milk source and culture lot for blended vats becomes excessively burdensome and clutters our standard tracking cards without adding meaningful safety value. We request that batch documentation allow summarizing complex milk blends and culture rotations under standard master batch identifiers.
std-102-1.0:CCC015AC-1247-5EA6-A662-FBE0.proposedChange: Change §1 to read: Make date, primary milk source or silo group, active culture lot or blend identifier, salting, each move between rooms, and the release date.
std-102-1.0:CCC015AC-1247-5EA6-A662-FBE0.response: The committee accepted the comment in principle. While detailed tracking remains vital, the wording is clarified in the next revision to permit master identifiers for blended milk silos and culture rotations, ensuring members maintain traceability without administrative overreach.

std-102-1.0:CCC015AC-1247-5EA6-A662-FBE0.comment: As a producer, I appreciate the flexibility of retaining records either on paper or through electronic formats. However, specifying that records must be kept for at least two years after the last wheel is sold should explicitly clarify that digital scans of paper logs satisfy this requirement to prevent local auditors from demanding original physical sheets.
std-102-1.0:CCC015AC-1247-5EA6-A662-FBE0.proposedChange: Clarify §2 by adding: electronic formats include scanned physical logs and verified database entries.
std-102-1.0:CCC015AC-1247-5EA6-A662-FBE0.response: The committee accepted the comment. The text is updated to explicitly note that scanned physical logs and database entries fully satisfy the electronic retention format option.

std-102-1.1:067065F5-7F1C-57F1-A0F8-92D7.comment: At Hazelcombe Cheesemonger we find that raw data-logger exports are far too messy to serve as reliable aging logs. Sensors glitch and drop packets, leaving gaps that require manual notation. Treating unedited raw dumps as official records creates compliance risks that inspectors will flag immediately during our routine audits.
std-102-1.1:067065F5-7F1C-57F1-A0F8-92D7.proposedChange: Require all raw data-logger exports to be transcribed and verified by a supervisor before being accepted as valid aging records.
std-102-1.1:067065F5-7F1C-57F1-A0F8-92D7.response: The committee declines the change. Raw data-logger and sensor exports provide a direct, untampered record of cave conditions. Requiring manual transcription introduces human error and potential record tampering, which is counter to the intent of verifying environmental controls during aging.

std-102-1.1:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9D48.comment: As a food safety consultant visiting various producers, I endorse this amendment. I suggest a minor wording polish to clarify that unedited refers specifically to the digital file structure rather than general record housekeeping.
std-102-1.1:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9D48.proposedChange: Insert digitally before unedited so it reads kept digitally unedited.
std-102-1.1:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9D48.response: The committee accepts the proposal. Adding the word digitally clarifies that the prohibition on editing applies to the electronic data file generated by the sensor system.

std-102-1.1:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.comment: At Herrera Farmstead, our digital temperature and humidity logs contain thousands of daily entries. Requiring every single exported data point to be printed for inspection creates an excessive paper burden and high printing costs without adding real food safety value.
std-102-1.1:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.proposedChange: Change can be printed on request to can be summarized in daily or weekly aggregate reports and printed on request.
std-102-1.1:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.response: The committee recognizes the volume of data generated by continuous loggers. We accept in principle that summaries may be maintained, provided the underlying unedited raw export remains accessible on the system for complete verification during audits.

std-102-1.1:A7494213-EBF3-5A89-8197-8657.comment: As a head cheesemonger receiving imported wheels, I support this flexible approach to electronic records. To make the sentence flow better for international readers, we should change printed on request to made available in printed form upon request.
std-102-1.1:A7494213-EBF3-5A89-8197-8657.proposedChange: Replace can be printed on request with can be made available in printed form upon request.
std-102-1.1:A7494213-EBF3-5A89-8197-8657.response: The committee rejects the requested wording change. The existing phrasing is direct, active, and easily understood by operators and auditors alike without adding unnecessary words.

std-102-1.1:AC73CCD5-783B-5A03-9A6B-3A97.comment: As herd manager at Pippinvale Farm, I fully support this amendment for modernizing our cave documentation. However, the phrase can be printed on request is slightly ambiguous regarding the required format and time frame. Specifying a PDF or CSV file format and a maximum response time for audits would improve clarity.
std-102-1.1:AC73CCD5-783B-5A03-9A6B-3A97.proposedChange: Change can be printed on request to can be exported as a PDF or CSV and printed within twenty-four hours of an inspector request.
std-102-1.1:AC73CCD5-783B-5A03-9A6B-3A97.response: The committee agrees that clarity on export formats is helpful. While we do not wish to mandate specific file extensions, the text is adjusted to state that exports must be printable in a standard human-readable format upon request.

std-102-1.1:EA083819-F4F1-5CD5-A43D-2CD3.comment: This is a sensible update that reflects current dairy operations. To improve readability and ensure consistent application across all ripening facilities, we should replace the word kept with maintained.
std-102-1.1:EA083819-F4F1-5CD5-A43D-2CD3.proposedChange: Replace kept unedited with maintained unedited in the text.
std-102-1.1:EA083819-F4F1-5CD5-A43D-2CD3.response: The committee accepts the editorial change. The word maintained is more precise and aligns better with standard terminology used across other ICF documentation.

std-103-1.0-r1:52640EB6-BBD5-5EA2-BDF1-1.comment: As an educator at Brackenfell Center for Cheese Studies, I find the reference to ICF-STD-101 §3 helpful, but the wording can be streamlined for better readability across our student materials and course handouts.
std-103-1.0-r1:52640EB6-BBD5-5EA2-BDF1-1.proposedChange: Replace 'recorded in its validated protocol under ICF-STD-101 §3' with 'documented under ICF-STD-101 §3'.
std-103-1.0-r1:52640EB6-BBD5-5EA2-BDF1-1.response: The committee agrees with the editorial tightening. The phrasing has been updated to improve clarity for training materials.

std-103-1.0-r1:5E9F2CDA-B022-53E7-AA02-F.comment: At Dubois Farmstead, we welcome the clarification on the 60-day floor, but the phrase 'each maker's reasons' sounds too informal for an official standards document. We should use professional terminology.
std-103-1.0-r1:5E9F2CDA-B022-53E7-AA02-F.proposedChange: Replace 'each maker's reasons' with 'the documented rationale of the producer'.
std-103-1.0-r1:5E9F2CDA-B022-53E7-AA02-F.response: The committee accepts this change to enhance the formal tone and professional precision of the standard.

std-103-1.0-r1:7FC09347-424D-5147-981B-C.comment: The 60-day floor is too restrictive for certain artisanal lactic goat cheeses produced in our region. We should strike the 60-day floor entirely and rely solely on individual validated protocols.
std-103-1.0-r1:7FC09347-424D-5147-981B-C.proposedChange: Remove the 60-day floor requirement from the text.
std-103-1.0-r1:7FC09347-424D-5147-981B-C.response: The committee rejects this comment because the 60-day floor is a fundamental baseline required to maintain baseline safety compliance across all member operations.

std-103-1.0-r1:83F1E1CF-8BDC-59B2-B3D5-E.comment: As a supplier operating across multiple regions, making the extended aging period merely recommended creates uneven market expectations. Buyers want uniform requirements, not optional guidelines that vary from creamery to creamery.
std-103-1.0-r1:83F1E1CF-8BDC-59B2-B3D5-E.proposedChange: Make the extended aging period mandatory for all soft and semi-soft sheep and goat cheeses.
std-103-1.0-r1:83F1E1CF-8BDC-59B2-B3D5-E.response: The committee rejects this comment because member practices and regional styles vary widely. A recommendation provides necessary flexibility while maintaining safety through the 60-day floor.

std-103-1.0-r1:856688F8-C895-5E8E-91F2-C.comment: In our creamery, we appreciate the distinction between the mandatory 60-day floor and the recommended longer aging for soft styles, but the hyphenation in semi-soft needs correction to align with our style guides.
std-103-1.0-r1:856688F8-C895-5E8E-91F2-C.proposedChange: Ensure consistent hyphenation for the term semi-soft throughout the paragraph.
std-103-1.0-r1:856688F8-C895-5E8E-91F2-C.response: The committee accepts this editorial correction to ensure consistent formatting throughout the standards document.

std-103-1.0-r1:89542F64-729C-5166-B18A-7.comment: Working at Rushfen Cheese Co., I noticed a minor grammatical ambiguity regarding whether the recommendation applies to the maker or the protocol. A slight restructuring will prevent any confusion during audits.
std-103-1.0-r1:89542F64-729C-5166-B18A-7.proposedChange: Revise the clause to read: 'with each maker recording its reasons in a validated protocol under ICF-STD-101 §3.'
std-103-1.0-r1:89542F64-729C-5166-B18A-7.response: The committee accepts this wording adjustment as it clarifies the responsibility of the maker in maintaining the protocol.

std-103-1.0-r1:9FE55C26-8983-53AA-B517-5.comment: At Foxcombe Creamery, we support the revised text. However, referencing ICF-STD-101 §3 directly at the end of the sentence feels slightly abrupt. Adding a comma before the cross-reference would improve readability.
std-103-1.0-r1:9FE55C26-8983-53AA-B517-5.proposedChange: Add a comma before the cross-reference to ICF-STD-101 §3.
std-103-1.0-r1:9FE55C26-8983-53AA-B517-5.response: The committee accepts the spirit of this suggestion and has adjusted the punctuation to improve the flow of the sentence.

std-103-1.0-r1:A7494213-EBF3-5A89-8197-8.comment: The text states that the 60-day floor applies, but for many traditional goat cheeses, this arbitrary duration does not reflect true moisture levels and safety parameters. We should allow alternative scientific validations instead of forcing a strict 60-day minimum across all styles.
std-103-1.0-r1:A7494213-EBF3-5A89-8197-8.proposedChange: Add an exemption to the 60-day floor for moisture-tested cheeses with a validated scientific safety protocol.
std-103-1.0-r1:A7494213-EBF3-5A89-8197-8.response: The committee rejects this comment because the 60-day minimum remains a baseline standard for safety across member states. Altering this fundamental floor is outside the scope of this annex.

std-103-1.0-r1:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C.comment: Requiring a validated protocol under ICF-STD-101 §3 imposes an undue administrative burden on small educational facilities like ours at Quillbrook Dairy Institute. We lack the staff resources to maintain formal documentation for every experimental batch.
std-103-1.0-r1:DBE0287D-6ABA-59B0-A251-C.response: The committee rejects this comment because documentation under ICF-STD-101 §3 is essential for traceability and safety assurance, and adequate guidance is provided for all production scales.

std-103-1.0-r1:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7.comment: At Wrenfield Creamery, our retail customers expect clarity on soft sheep and goat cheeses. Leaving the extended aging period merely recommended makes it difficult for mongers to explain variations in maturity. The protocol should explicitly mandate documentation of the aging duration to protect quality.
std-103-1.0-r1:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7.proposedChange: Change the recommendation for soft and semi-soft styles to a mandatory requirement for documented aging periods.
std-103-1.0-r1:FD8E23C5-F87D-556B-B4CA-7.response: The committee agrees that clarity is essential for mongers and producers alike. We accept the change to require explicit documentation of the aging duration within the validated protocol.

std-103-1.0:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9D48.comment: From a food safety consulting perspective, a blanket 90-day requirement lacks empirical backing for lower-moisture goat cheeses. The federal floor is fully protective when combined with standard pasteurization or moisture controls.
std-103-1.0:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9D48.proposedChange: Replace the 90-day rule with the 60-day federal floor.
std-103-1.0:072EC674-2A47-5F88-8AD1-9D48.response: The committee accepted the principle of the comment, aligning the standard with the federal floor to address safety and seasonal viability concerns raised across the membership.

std-103-1.0:220E1A3F-4B9F-5D59-8B6A-8A4B.comment: As a cheese buyer at Orchardmere Cheese Co., I appreciate the simplicity of applying ICF-STD-101. However, the reference could explicitly state the version number of the base standard to avoid any ambiguity during retail distribution audits.
std-103-1.0:220E1A3F-4B9F-5D59-8B6A-8A4B.proposedChange: Change to: Applies ICF-STD-101 version 2.0 to cheese made from sheep or goat milk.
std-103-1.0:220E1A3F-4B9F-5D59-8B6A-8A4B.response: The committee notes the writer withdrew the comment after discussing the scope during the chapter meet-up, agreeing that standard numbering conventions already cover base document references.

std-103-1.0:220E1A3F-4B9F-5D59-8B6A-8A4B.comment: Requiring 90 days for raw-milk sheep and goat cheese creates unnecessary inventory stagnation for our retail counters without adding proven food safety benefits beyond the 60-day federal floor. We should align with standard aging practices.
std-103-1.0:220E1A3F-4B9F-5D59-8B6A-8A4B.proposedChange: Replace 90 days with the federal 60-day floor for raw-milk cheese.
std-103-1.0:220E1A3F-4B9F-5D59-8B6A-8A4B.response: The committee accepted the comment because members agreed the evidence for a 90-day requirement is insufficient and creates severe hardship for short milking seasons. The section will be revised.

std-103-1.0:220E1A3F-4B9F-5D59-8B6A-8A4B.comment: Allowing frozen sheep-milk curd is a welcome flexibility for seasonal producers. To ensure complete traceability for retail buyers, we should specify that the freeze date must appear clearly on both the make record and the master inventory log.
std-103-1.0:220E1A3F-4B9F-5D59-8B6A-8A4B.proposedChange: Amend to require the freeze date in the make record and master inventory log.
std-103-1.0:220E1A3F-4B9F-5D59-8B6A-8A4B.response: The committee accepted the change to improve inventory traceability for buyers, noting that adding the master inventory log strengthens recordkeeping without burdening producers.

std-103-1.0:2266EC81-CDCD-5C2D-A2DC-4362.comment: The section permits frozen sheep-milk curd but would benefit from specifying exactly where the freeze date must be recorded within the make record for better auditability.
std-103-1.0:2266EC81-CDCD-5C2D-A2DC-4362.proposedChange: Specify that the freeze date must be entered prominently in the lot header of the make record.
std-103-1.0:2266EC81-CDCD-5C2D-A2DC-4362.response: The committee accepted the editorial comment, adding clarifying instructions on where to log the freeze date to ensure smooth compliance audits.

std-103-1.0:38462C1A-999E-520E-BE56-FA3F.comment: As an affineur working with diverse batches, applying the base standard to mixed milks is straightforward. However, terminology around mixed species percentages could be slightly tighter.
std-103-1.0:38462C1A-999E-520E-BE56-FA3F.proposedChange: Clarify mixed milks as containing at least twenty percent sheep or goat milk.
std-103-1.0:38462C1A-999E-520E-BE56-FA3F.response: The committee noted the withdrawal of this comment following discussion during the chapter meet-up regarding mixed-milk definitions.

std-103-1.0:38462C1A-999E-520E-BE56-FA3F.comment: Permitting frozen sheep-milk curd is a major change for traditional affineurs. We need more guidance on traceability and moisture loss differences in cheese made from frozen curd before finalizing this clause.
std-103-1.0:38462C1A-999E-520E-BE56-FA3F.proposedChange: Defer this section to allow time for industry studies on frozen curd aging characteristics.
std-103-1.0:38462C1A-999E-520E-BE56-FA3F.response: The committee deferred this comment for consideration in the next revision of the document, pending further technical data on moisture retention in frozen curd cheeses.

std-103-1.0:52640EB6-BBD5-5EA2-BDF1-14F2.comment: Teaching cheese science requires regulatory clarity. The 90-day requirement creates confusion against the federal floor without providing documented public health benefits.
std-103-1.0:52640EB6-BBD5-5EA2-BDF1-14F2.proposedChange: Replace the 90-day requirement with the standard federal floor.
std-103-1.0:52640EB6-BBD5-5EA2-BDF1-14F2.response: The committee accepted the comment, agreeing that educational programs and producers alike benefit from clear alignment with the federal floor, and the text will be updated.

std-103-1.0:5544CB6B-86DC-58AE-B998-01B7.comment: The proposed 90-day aging period ignores the economic reality of seasonal dairy operations and exceeds the federal floor without supporting data. We must revert to standard timelines for small ruminants.
std-103-1.0:5544CB6B-86DC-58AE-B998-01B7.proposedChange: Remove the 90-day requirement and adopt the 60-day federal floor.
std-103-1.0:5544CB6B-86DC-58AE-B998-01B7.response: The committee accepted the principle of aligning with members' operational realities, resolving to revise the aging requirement to match the federal floor while adding guidance on moisture testing.

std-103-1.0:5E9F2CDA-B022-53E7-AA02-F23E.comment: At Dubois Farmstead, our goat milk production is entirely seasonal. Forcing a ninety-day aging period disrupts our cash flow and conflicts with traditional practices without adding measurable safety benefits.
std-103-1.0:5E9F2CDA-B022-53E7-AA02-F23E.proposedChange: Revise the draft to set the mandatory aging period at sixty days for all raw-milk sheep and goat cheeses.
std-103-1.0:5E9F2CDA-B022-53E7-AA02-F23E.response: The committee accepted the principle of this comment by recognizing the economic impact on seasonal producers, and the item will be restructured for the subsequent revision.

std-103-1.0:65AD0562-1908-540C-937D-2BC2.comment: At Wrenfield Fine Cheese, we believe specialized sheep and goat products require extended aging to ensure pathogen reduction and develop distinct regional flavor profiles. Reverting to sixty days weakens the standard.
std-103-1.0:65AD0562-1908-540C-937D-2BC2.proposedChange: Modify §A2 to mandate the ninety-day aging period for all raw-milk sheep and goat cheese varieties.
std-103-1.0:65AD0562-1908-540C-937D-2BC2.response: The committee rejected this comment because the ballot item failed, and feedback from the wider membership indicated insufficient evidence to support a mandatory ninety-day period over the federal floor.

std-103-1.0:66D713AB-A42E-5EFB-AF8B-DA62.comment: The section permitting frozen sheep-milk curd is clear and beneficial for our seasonal cheesemaking courses, but the cross-reference to make records lacks a specific timeframe for how long freeze dates must be retained. For educational clarity in our training materials, we should specify the retention period.
std-103-1.0:66D713AB-A42E-5EFB-AF8B-DA62.proposedChange: Change the text to read: Allows frozen sheep-milk curd to be used, with its freeze date recorded in the make record and retained for at least 12 months.
std-103-1.0:66D713AB-A42E-5EFB-AF8B-DA62.response: The committee accepted the editorial suggestion to clarify record retention for frozen curd. The clause will be updated in the revised draft to explicitly state that the freeze date must be maintained in the make record for a minimum of 12 months.

std-103-1.0:72A4DA25-C472-5D86-81EA-DDCF.comment: At Rushfen Creamery Cooperative, we find the scope clear regarding mixed milks. I am submitting an editorial note to ensure the term mixed milks is consistently capitalized throughout the document text.
std-103-1.0:72A4DA25-C472-5D86-81EA-DDCF.proposedChange: Capitalize Mixed Milks when referring to blended species batches.
std-103-1.0:72A4DA25-C472-5D86-81EA-DDCF.response: The committee notes the writer withdrew the comment after it was clarified that lowercase usage conforms to the stylistic guidelines of the International Cheese Federation style guide.

std-103-1.0:73619338-F1FC-50C4-8C4A-3585.comment: As a retailer, clear make records including freeze dates help us communicate provenance to customers. The wording is sound, but adding a specific record retention duration will improve compliance.
std-103-1.0:73619338-F1FC-50C4-8C4A-3585.proposedChange: Amend §A3 to specify that freeze dates must be retained in make records for a minimum of two years.
std-103-1.0:73619338-F1FC-50C4-8C4A-3585.response: The committee accepted the editorial suggestion to specify the record retention timeframe for frozen sheep-milk curd batches.

std-103-1.0:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.comment: At Herrera Farmstead, our retail selection relies on seasonal sheep and goat cheeses coming to market reliably. Imposing a 90-day aging requirement rather than aligning with the standard federal floor creates severe supply bottlenecks without offering tangible safety benefits.
std-103-1.0:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.proposedChange: Align the aging period for raw-milk sheep and goat cheese directly with the standard federal floor.
std-103-1.0:74C2B126-78E7-5C93-BEA8-E048.response: The committee accepted the comment, noting that forcing a 90-day requirement creates undue supply pressures for retailers without substantiated microbiological evidence, and will revise the draft accordingly.

std-103-1.0:755D763F-EF70-5105-8C95-5FE8.comment: As a committee member, I find the cross-reference to ICF-STD-101 too ambiguous when applied to mixed-milk cheeses containing varying ratios of bovine, ovine, and caprine milk. We need clearer guidance on threshold percentages.
std-103-1.0:755D763F-EF70-5105-8C95-5FE8.proposedChange: Clarify that mixed milks apply when sheep or goat milk exceeds fifty percent of the total volume.
std-103-1.0:755D763F-EF70-5105-8C95-5FE8.response: The committee accepted the comment in principle, agreeing that mixed-milk thresholds need clarification, and will add an explanatory note referencing standard dairy accounting rather than a strict 50 percent rule.

std-103-1.0:755D763F-EF70-5105-8C95-5FE8.comment: The 90-day aging mandate in §A2 lacks scientific backing and conflicts with standard industry practices for seasonal goat-milk production, threatening specialty product availability across our retail network.
std-103-1.0:755D763F-EF70-5105-8C95-5FE8.proposedChange: Strike the 90-day rule and align the aging period with the federal floor.
std-103-1.0:755D763F-EF70-5105-8C95-5FE8.response: The committee accepted the comment, noting the extensive feedback from producers and retailers regarding short milking seasons, and will remove the 90-day requirement in the revised draft.

std-103-1.0:83F1E1CF-8BDC-59B2-B3D5-E88E.comment: The text as drafted demands raw-milk sheep or goat cheese to be aged at least 90 days, beyond the 60-day floor, without adequate pathogen survival data specific to small ruminant milks. Our suppliers in the Jura region find this extra restriction unsupported by microbiological evidence from our annual competition entries and commercial batches.
std-103-1.0:83F1E1CF-8BDC-59B2-B3D5-E88E.proposedChange: Amend the requirement to state that raw-milk sheep and goat cheese shall be aged for not less than the 60-day federal floor, matching standard pathogen reduction timelines.
std-103-1.0:83F1E1CF-8BDC-59B2-B3D5-E88E.response: The committee accepted the technical concern in principle. While the 90-day requirement is removed due to lack of definitive pathogen evidence, the text will be revised to align strictly with the federal floor pending a comprehensive review of moisture and acid development in small ruminant cheeses.

std-103-1.0:856688F8-C895-5E8E-91F2-CDF1.comment: The scope phrasing is mostly clear, but adding a precise reference number to the base standard will help avoid any confusion for inspectors reviewing mixed-milk batches at our creamery.
std-103-1.0:856688F8-C895-5E8E-91F2-CDF1.proposedChange: Update §A2 to read: Applies ICF-STD-101 provisions explicitly to cheese made from sheep or goat milk, and from mixed milks.
std-103-1.0:856688F8-C895-5E8E-91F2-CDF1.response: The committee accepted the proposed editorial clarification to improve cross-document consistency and make the scope explicit for mixed-milk cheeses.

std-103-1.0:958B1085-3310-588F-AAC0-31AA.comment: Our production schedules cannot absorb an arbitrary 90-day aging window. The federal floor provides adequate safety controls, and extending it without clear data penalizes small sheep and goat dairies.
std-103-1.0:958B1085-3310-588F-AAC0-31AA.proposedChange: Adopt the standard federal floor for raw-milk sheep and goat cheeses.
